sam_infra: Heads up — we saw a p95 east-west latency spike between gpu-nodes in eu-west-1 during the 11:30-12:00 batch window. Graphs show sudden 40-120ms jumps for ~5m across multiple racks.
anya_sre: saw same on our alerting. Packet loss counters edged up ~0.8-1.5% on mlx5 interfaces at the same time. No correlated CPU or GPU saturation.
kai_neteng: any RDMA fallbacks in the logs? paste from node pair would help.
sam_infra: yes — logs show a few RDMA QP resets and then immediate fallback to TCP for the affected flows. Snippet:
```
[11:34:12] rdma: qp 0x3a reset -> fallback_to_tcp
[11:34:13] mlx5: tx err 4 cnt++ interface=eth1
[11:34:14] net: rto-heavy retransmit -> p95 jumps
```
jules_prod: these were peak batching bursts — lots of small seq lengths (8-32 tokens) causing many short-lived flows. Our continuous batching + KV cache made lots of simultaneous connections between the same node pairs.
kai_neteng: interesting — short flows hurt ECMP hashing, causes reordering on multi-path switches. Could be path asymmetry + small MTU frames triggering frag retries on some ToR. What MTU are you running?
sam_infra: 9000 across racks. But counters show some fragments and 'out_of_order_frag' on a few ToRs.
anya_sre: also noticed an uptick in tail latency across dedicated pods pinned to those racks. Canary routing to other racks lowered p95 by ~30ms.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: rolling NIC firmware update completed on rack 12 at 11:50 (success)
kai_neteng: plan suggestion: 1) isolate one bad ToR pair and run tcpdump + pcap on both ToRs during next window, 2) temporarily reduce ECMP bin count to force fewer paths for short flows, 3) enable RDMA debug level on one node pair to capture QP lifecycle, 4) schedule NIC firmware/driver bump for other racks if pattern repeats.
jules_prod: for immediate mitigation can we route high-QPS batch traffic to dedicated capacity in us-east while we debug? That will cost more but avoids customer impact.
sam_infra: agreed — have started a canary migration for the highest 3 tenants to dedicated pools. Monitoring now.
anya_sre: also propose adding a KV cache warmup to reduce simultaneous cold-fanout across many node pairs during window — if we can spread warmup earlier it reduces short-flow storm.
kai_neteng: one more thought: check MTU auto-negotiation on the inter-rack spine links. If one side silently drops jumbo or changes min-frag this creates intermittent fragmentation at peak throughput.
sam_infra: added MTU/fragmentation telemetry to our packet-exporter. Will run a focused sweep during the next predicted batch window (tomorrow 11:30). Anyone want to join live debug?
anya_sre: I will. Also prepping rollback playbook if firmware change worsens.
jules_prod: I'll keep customers informed — flagging potential cost bump for routing to dedicated pools: estimated +12-18% for the hour of canary.
ops-bot: incident-tracker: created ticket INF-2026-391 for batch-window east-west latency spike, assigned to eng-infra oncall.
sam_infra: thanks — next steps: live packet captures, ECMP bin tweak, RDMA debug run, and decision on wider NIC firmware rollout after reproduction. Meeting in #eng-infra-debug at 11:20 tomorrow. :mag:
kai_neteng: I'll prepare a quick script to correlate QP resets with ECMP path hashes and ToR counters. See you all tomorrow.
anya_sre: nice troubleshooting thread. :thumbsup:
